Commentary.Commentary: So, that's it from this one-off Test. Bangladesh have prevailed over the visitors and now the action switches to white ball cricket. Now, Bangladesh take on Zimbabwe in the 1st of the 3-match ODI series which begins on 1st March 2020 at 1300 local (0700 GMT). Till then take care and cheers!!!

Bangladesh skipper, Mominul Haque says that sometimes as a captain we have to adjust with the difficulty start to the career. He further says that the  guys played well as a team. He praises Nayeem Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim and Najmul Hasan for their efforts. He adds that he is happy to score some runs and contribute to the teams cause. He ends by saying that the boys are eager to play some white ball cricket and hopes that they win there too.

For his brilliant unbeaten knock of 203 runs  Mushfiqur Rahim is adjudged as the Man Of The Match. He says that they badly needed a win as they lost the last 6 matches they played previously. He praises Najmul Hasan Shanto for playing brilliantly. He further says that he was lucky to make it big and get to a double ton. He mentions that they played well in all the three departments. Further says that he hopes to repeat this performace in coming games.

Zimbabwe skipper, Craig Ervine says that it was nice to get runs but he says that he looks to take the positives from this game. He also says that they got starts but failed to convert them.  Further says that the bowlers did not hit the right lines and lengths as compared to their Bangladesh counterparts who made them work hard for the runs. He also says that they work hard to gain the momentum but throw it away by poor shot selection.
In the end, poor batting, poor bowling and poor fielding resulted them ending on a losing side and that too getting humiliated with an innings loss. Stay tuned for the presentations...

As far Bangladesh's batting is concerned Saif Hassan departed cheaply but a 78-run stand between the experienced Tamim Iqbal and Najmul Hasan Shanto revived their innings. Tamim departed in the 40's and then Najmul Hasan Shanto followed him after a well compiled 71 runs. Then came a marathon partnership of 222 runs between Mushfiqur Rahim and Mominul Haque. The duo reached to their respective tons too. The latter though departed but the former reached to his double ton. In the end, Bangladesh ended up gaining a massive 295-run lead. Talking of the Zimbabwe bowlers they were poor in their approach. Dishing out freebies and that just did not do justice to them as they struggled to take wickets regularly.

Coming to the match, Zimbabwe won the toss and chose to bat. They put on 265 in the first innings courtesy a 111-run stand between skipper Craig Ervine and Prince Masvuare. Masvaure though was dismissed in the 60's but Ervine continued to play his game and eventually got to his 3rd Test ton. His departure soon opened the floodgates. For Bangladesh, Nayeem Hasan and Abu Jayed both took 4 wickets apiece to restrict Zimbabwe under 270.

Soon after the Lunch break, Zimbabwe lost Sikandar Raza who was batting well on 47 but a brilliant effort in the field from Mushfiqur Rahim saw him heading back to the pavilion. After that it was just a matter of time as till when can Zimbabwe avoid the inevitable. Timycen Maruma played fearlessly as he made 41 but lacked support at the other end. Once Maruma got dismissed the game was over there and then. Nayeem Hasan was the chief destroyer as he took 5 wickets in this innings and was ably supported by Taijul Islam who also took 4 wickets.

A thumping win for the Bangla Tigers. They have broken their 6-match losing streak in the longest format. They were brilliant and clinical in their approach. 9 wickets taken by spinners tells the story in itself. Bangladesh began the day superbly by strangling the run flow and picking a couple of quick wickets early on before a 60-run stand between Sikandar Raza and Craig Ervine revived slightest of hope for the visitors. But Skipper, Ervine's wicket at the stroke of Lunch snatched away all the momentum they had got.

We are back for the second session. The Bangladesh players are out in the middle. Sikandar Raza and Timycen Maruma will resume their batting for Zimbabwe. Nayeem Hasan will start the proceedings for this session.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

27 overs, 105 runs and 3 wickets is what we got in this session. Off the two teams, Bangladesh would be the happier of the two. The day started with Bangladesh bowling some tight lines and lengths to eke out 3 maidens first up. Taijul started from where he left on Day 3 as he struck in his 3rd over of the day as he accounted for opener Kevin Kasuza. Then came Nayeem Hasan to the scene and he got the wicket of Brendan Taylor off his first over of the day. After that Bangladesh's bowling looked a bit haywire as runs started to flow when Craig Ervine and Sikandar Raza were in the middle. The duo added 60 for the 5th wicket but Ervine had to take the long walk back just before the Lunch Break courtesy of his Bangladesh counterpart's brilliant direct hit. Zimbabwe still trail by 181 runs and have just 5 wickets in their bag. Bangladesh have been brilliant with the ball so far especially the spinners and they would look to wrap up the Zimbabwean innings in the post Lunch session. Do join us at 1210 local (0610 GMT) for the post Lunch session.

Sikandar Raza is the next batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Hasan has accounted for Taylor for the second time in this match. Superb bowling from the youngster. He tosses one around middle, Taylor goes for the big slog on the leg side but ends up getting a top edge towards deep square leg where Taijul Islam runs forward and takes an excellent catch. Zimbabwe still trail by 251!
Floated on middle and leg, Ervine tucks it towards mid-wicket and gets a single.
Floated and on the pads, Taylor flicks it to the leg side and gets a single.

FOUR BYES! Ervine escapes once again playing the reverse sweep. It is the same shot that led to his downfall in the first innings. Hasan bowls it full and outside off, Taylor goes for the reverse sweep but he fails to get wood to the ball as it sneaks under it. It also beats the keeper as it races to the fence at fine leg for a boundary.
Floated around off and middle, Taylor keeps it out on the leg side off the back foot.
Finally the wait is over as Nayeem Hasan will bowl for the first time on Day 4. So far he has been impressive with figures of 3-1-4-2.
Short of a length ball outside off, Ervine stands tall and punches the ball off the back foot towards covers.
Length and on middle and leg, Ervine tucks it off the back foot towards fine leg and scampers back for a couple.
Dishes one more wide outside off, Ervine is not interested to play at it.
Hossain bowls one in the channel outside off, Ervine won't fall in the trap as he shoulders arms to it.
On a good length on off, Ervine keeps it out.
FOUR! Terrific shot! Short and outside off, Ervine cuts it hard through point for a boundary.
Tossed up around off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
Flighted and on off, Taylor keeps it out off the back foot.

SIX! Taylor is not going to hold back here. He will take the attack to the opposition. Islam floats one around off, Taylor takes a few steps down the track and lofts it cleanly over long off for a biggie.
Floated ball on off, Taylor keeps it out off the back foot.
Full around off, Taylor drives it towards long on and gets to the other end.
Flatter and outside off, Taylor plays it off the back foot through cover-point and gets a run.
Good length and outside off, Ervine leaves it to see off the over.

Short of a length ball on leg, Ervine looks to flick it to the leg side but gets beaten on the flick and is rapped high on the pads. The ball rolls to the leg side as the bowler appeals. The umpire shakes his head.
Length and on middle, Ervine blocks it off the back foot towards mid on.
Another good length ball and outside off, Ervine makes a leave once again.
Length ball outside off, Ervine lets it go.

FOUR! The Zimbabwe skipper gets a boundary. Bonus runs there. Hossain bowls one on a length and takes it away from the batter. Ervine stands tall and guides it through the vacant gully region and fetches a boundary.
Ebadot Hossain is on.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Taylor looks to defend but gets hit on the pads.
Floated delivery on middle, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
Short delivery on off, Taylor makes room and punches it through covers. The batsmen get two runs.
Loopy delivery on leg, Taylor sweeps it towards fine leg. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Flighted delivery outside off, Taylor leaves it alone.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Ervine flicks it through square leg for a single.
Outside off, Brendan offers no shot to this one.
Full delivery on off, Taylor pushes it to covers.
On a length on middle, Taylor pushes it towards mid on.
On a good length on off, Taylor keeps it out.
Good length delivery on off, Brendan defends it off the back foot.
On a good length on middle, Taylor flicks it to mid-wicket.
Another ball that is tossed up around off, Ervine lunges forward and defends it off the inside half of his bat towards the leg side.
Floated around off, Ervine keeps it out off the  front foot.
Craig Ervine, the skipper, is the new batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Taijul strikes and Zimbabwe are three down. Brilliantly bowled from Taijul. He was constantly bowling around middle and leg and this time too he bowls a similar line. Kasuza looks to turn it on the leg side but gets squared up as he closes the bat face early. The ball takes the shoulder of the bat and flies towards the slip cordon where the second slip fielder Mohammad Mithun takes the catch. Zimbabwe still trail by 280 runs!
Floated around off, Kasuza lunges forward and defends it.
Floated and on middle and leg, Kasuza keeps it out off the front foot.
Flatter and shorter outside off, Kasuza gets on top of the bounce and pulls it all along the ground towards mid-wicket. Does not get it off the middle of the bat but will get a couple.
Short of a length ball on middle, Taylor keeps it out off the back foot.
On a length and outside off, Taylor shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Delightful shot! First runs of the morning and what a way to get that. Jayed overpitches one outside off, Taylor drives it from the sweet part of the bat and the ball races through covers for a boundary with a lightning speed.
On a good length but way outside off, Taylor leaves it.
Length and around middle, Taylor keeps it out off the inside half of the bat towards mid on.
Length ball outside off, Taylor drives it towards covers where the fielder dives to his left and saves a certain boundary.
Full and on off, driven straight to the man at covers.
Flighted ball on off, Kasuza blocks it off the  front foot towards the off side.
Floated ball on leg, Kasuza turns it towards the man at short leg.
Tossed up on middle, Kevin pushes it off the front foot.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Kasuza defends it off the front foot towards the leg side.
Floated on off, Kasuza keeps it out off the front foot.
On a good length on off, Brendan blocks it off the back foot. Third maiden on the trot for Bangladesh.
Full delivery on middle, Brendan plays it towards mid on.
On a good length on off, Taylor keeps it out.
Full delivery on off, Taylor drives it towards mid off.
Good length delivery on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
On a good length and outside off, Taylor shoulders arms to this one.
Full and angled into the pads, Kasuza flicks it to mid-wicket. A maiden for Taijul to begin with.

OHH! Almost a wicket there. Taijul is bowling superbly. He tosses one up around off and gives some air to it, Kasuza looks to defend it off the back foot but ends up getting a thick outside edge which drops just short of the only slip fielder.
Tossed up around off and spinning in, Kasuza looks to defend it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Floated ball on off, Kasuza gets forward and defends it off the higher part of the bat. Some extra bounce on this one for Taijul.
Another one which is bowled shorter and Kasuza defends it off the back foot.
Flatter one on middle, Kasuza punches it off the back foot.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end.
Fuller in length and on off, Taylor drives it to covers. A maiden to start for Abu Jayed.
On a fuller length and around off, Jayed looks to work it on the leg side but ends up getting an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls to the off side.
The floodlights have been put on as it is very dark at the moment.
Play and a miss! Brilliantly bowled from Jayed. He slips one on a length and makes the ball to swing away from the batter. Taylor plays it away from the body and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Short of a length ball around off, Taylor hangs on the back foot and plays the ball to point.
Fuller in length and around off, Taylor keeps it out off the back foot towards covers.
Jayed starts with a full delivery on off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.

We are all set to begin Day 4. The Bangladesh players are out in the middle. Kevin Kasuza and Brendan Taylor will resume their batting for Zimbabwe. Abu Jayed will start the proceedings for the hosts.

Pitch Report - Tino Mawoyo is down for the pitch report. He starts by saying that the pitch has dried up considerably and that has brought the spinners into the game. Mentions that the cracks have started to open up. He further states that the odd ball is keeping low especially from the pacers. Further adds that the Zimbabwe batsmen might come down the wicket to counter the variable bounce.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 which could probably be the final day of this one-off Test match between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Mirpur. Bangladesh earlier on Day 3 batted brilliantly when former captain, Mushfiqur Rahim and current captain, Mominul Haque both batted in tandem to push Zimbabwe out of the game by amassing a lead of 295 runs. The duo stitched a 222-run stand and reached their respective tons too. Though the latter failed to continue, the former went onto score a double ton, his 3rd in this format. The visitors started on a bad note as they lost 2 quick wickets before the close of play. The hosts today would look to take the remaining wickets quickly and wrap up the Test match. Nayeem Hasan will again be the key for them along with other bowlers. On the other hand, Zimbabwe would look to take it session by session and will look to delay the inevitable. Stay tuned for all the action which begins shortly...
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

What to speak of Zimbabwe, they needed to bat out just 5 overs but failed to do that miserably. They lost the wicket of Prince Masvaure and the nightwatchman, Donald Tiripano in the first over. Brendan Taylor and Kevin Kasuza managed to bat out the remaining overs but they still have a lot of work to do. On Day 4, they will look to survive for as long as possible and hope that the rain which is predicted on Days 4 and 5 arrive. Join us on Tuesday, 25th February, for what might be the last day of this Test match at 0930 Local (0330 GMT). Until then, take care.

What a brilliant day it has been for Bangladesh! They started the day on top and have ended it in the same manner. With the way they have performed, the game looks likely to end on Day 4 itself. After declaring the innings on a massive 560/6, courtesy Rahim's double ton and Mominul Haque's century, the bowlers gave a dream start to the hosts. Nayeem Hasan was brilliant with the ball in the first over as he picked up back-to-back wickets and that's what has set up a Day 4 finish in all likelihood. Bangladesh would look to pick the remaining wickets and aim to finish the game on Tuesday itself.
Flatter ball to end the day! Kasuza defends it out to short leg. STUMPS ON DAY 3.
Floated ball on off, Kasuza looks to defend but it hits the pads. There is a stifled appeal for LBW but nothing from the umpire.
On middle, blocked out.
EDGY! Floated ball on off, Kasuza looks to defend but it takes the outside edge  and goes towards  first slip. The fielder there dives and makes a good stop.
On middle, Kasuza defends it out.
Flatter one on middle, Kasuza flicks it to the fine leg region for a couple.
Almost dragged on! Flatter on off, Taylor looks to defend but it takes the bottom edge and hits the body of Taylor.
Loopy delivery on middle, Kasuza works it to square leg for a single.
Tosses this one up on middle, Kasuza flicks it to mid-wicket.
Full on middle, KK pushes it back to the bowler.
Floated on off, Kasuza prods forward and defends it out.
Looped up ball on middle, Kevin defends it out.
Full on middle, Taylor flicks it to mid on.
Flatter one on middle, Taylor defends it out.
Looped up ball on middle, Taylor blocks it out to the leg side.
Loopy delivery on middle, Taylor prods forward and defends it out.
Shorter in length outside off, Kasuza punches it off the back foot to deep cover for a single.
Flighted ball on off, Taylor looks to defend but it takes the inside edge and rolls to square leg. A single.
Flatter one on middle, Kasuza flicks it to the deep square leg region for a couple.
Loopy delivery on off, Kasuza defends it off the front foot.
On middle, Kasuza blocks it out onto the pitch.
Loopy delivery on middle, Kevin prods forward and defends it out.
Flatter one on off, Kasuza looks to defend off the back foot but it takes the outside edge and the ball goes towards the third man region for a couple.
BEATEN! Flighted one outside off, Kasuza looks to defend but fails to get any bat on it.
Taijul Islam will bowl from the other end.
Tossed up ball on middle, Taylor blocks it out. A sensational opening over from Nayeem Hasan!
Loopy one on middle, Taylor defends it out.
Floated on middle, Taylor defends it out.

OUT! CAUGHT! What is happening? Two wickets in two balls! Tiripano has to go now and it is all happening here in Bangladesh. Brilliant stuff from Hasan and Das. Flatter one outside off, Tiripano looks to defend off the back foot. It takes the outside edge and goes to the keeper who takes a very good catch. Brendan Taylor is the new man in.
Donald Tiripano is the next man in.

OUT! TIMBER! What a start for Bangladesh! Nayeem Hasan has given the hosts a dream beginning. Floated delivery on off, Masvaure looks to defend off the front foot but the ball straightedns after pitching, beating the inside edge of the bat and going onto hit the off stump.
Hasan starts with a flatter one outside off, Masvaure leaves the ball alone.
